title: Note on the local calculation of decoherence of quantum superposition in the static black holes
authors: Ran Li, Zhong-Xiao Man, Jin Wang
abstract: We investigate the decoherence of a quantum spatial superposition of a static particle in Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström black holes. By treating the particle as a localized classical source coupled to a quantum scalar field, we reformulate the decoherence process in the Danielson-Satishchandran-Wald (DSW) gedankenexperiment through coherent state generation and derive the local expression for the decoherence functional in terms of the Wightman function. In the long-time limit, the decoherence rate is shown to be characterized by the low-frequency behavior of the Wightman function. We then employ the asymptotic matching method to calculate the analytical expressions of the Wightman functions in the Boulware, Unruh, and Hartle-Hawking vacua. We show that the decoherence behavior depends on the quantum state of the environmental field. While the Boulware vacuum gives vanishing decoherence for a static superposition, the thermal effects associated with Hawking radiation in the Unruh and Hartle-Hawking vacua can induce nonvanishing decoherence.
summary: This theoretical paper calculates the rate at which a quantum superposition decays due to coupling with a scalar field near black holes. By analyzing different vacuum states—Boulware, Unruh, and Hartle-Hawking—the authors show that only thermal effects associated with Hawking radiation induce measurable decoherence. This demonstrates the profound dependence of quantum coherence on the chosen description of the spacetime environment.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum spatial superpositions of a particle decohere when coupled to a quantum scalar field in the curved spacetime backgrounds of static black holes (Schwarzschild and Reissner-Nordström).
main_result: Decoherence is found to vanish in the Boulware vacuum but is induced by thermal effects associated with Hawking radiation in Unruh and Hartle-Hawking vacua, yielding a non-zero rate even for extremal black holes.
method: The decoherence functional is derived locally using coherent state generation techniques, relating the rate to the low-frequency behavior of the Wightman function calculated via asymptotic matching methods.
model_or_system: The system models a quantum superposition of a static particle coupled to a real scalar field ($\Phi$) in curved spacetime. The analysis uses the interaction Hamiltonian derived from the coupling $S_{int} = \lambda \int d	au \Phi(x(	au))$.
key_observables: Decoherence functional, entanglement particle number $\langle N angle$, and the decoherence rate ($\Gamma$).
important_parameters: Black hole mass ($M$), charge ($Q$), coupling constant ($\lambda$), separation distance ($d$), and vacuum choice (Boulware, Unruh, Hartle-Hawking).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations such as treating the interaction profile as rectangular and using asymptotic matching methods for mode functions in different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the DSW gedankenexperiment, develops the coherent state formalism and local rate expression, applies it to Schwarzschild black holes, extends the analysis to Reissner-Nordström black holes, and concludes by summarizing the vacuum dependence.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete calculation of decoherence in curved spacetime environments, linking fundamental concepts like Hawking radiation and quantum field theory in curved spacetime directly to open quantum system dynamics (decoherence).
